purpose: Give learners a dated method for reading the AI regulatory environment by jurisdiction, actor, system, purpose, consequence, effective date, and enforcement status.
staffSummary: Build M28 around one consequential utility situation and one decision: Determine which legal or policy questions require qualified review for a proposed utility use case. The learner must leave with a usable AI regulatory applicability map, not a collection of definitions.
openingSituation: A vendor says its product is compliant with AI law, but the statement does not name the jurisdiction, provision, role, system use, or effective date.
learnerDecision: Determine which legal or policy questions require qualified review for a proposed utility use case.
analogy: A permit matrix shows which requirement applies to which activity and date. Regulation needs the same disciplined mapping.
learnerOutcomes: Explain The AI Regulation Landscape in plain English and connect it to a real water, wastewater, stormwater, or One Water decision.
Distinguish law, regulation, executive action, guidance, standard, proposal, effective date, and applicability without using one term to hide several different jobs.
Analyze the module situation, identify missing evidence, and name the professional consequence of a weak decision.
Compare how the same question changes across drinking water, wastewater, stormwater, administration, engineering, finance, technology, and public leadership.

curriculumOutcomes: Give The AI Regulation Landscape one clear learning job inside Governance, Security and Provenance.
Connect the module to a consequential decision and the AI regulatory applicability map.
Preserve current content, proposals, enhancements, and contributor records by stable identifier.
Separate verified evidence, Hardeep positions, expert interpretation, instructional scenarios, and unresolved questions.

marketingOutcomes: Describe the practical value as helping a learner make and explain this decision: Determine which legal or policy questions require qualified review for a proposed utility use case.
Name the AI regulatory applicability map as the visible result of the module.
Do not promise savings, compliance, certification, safety, performance, implementation success, or career outcomes without separately approved evidence.
definitionOfDone: The learner explains the core distinctions, completes the required evidence and decision activities, passes distributed checks, saves a complete AI regulatory applicability map, and names the next accountable action.
